title: Chapter 2 Review & Practice Test
overview: Pull the whole chapter together. This review revisits every section — division and the remainder theorem, the factor theorem, polynomial equations, families of functions, and polynomial inequalities — with mixed problems in the style of the chapter review and practice test. Use it to find your weak spots before a test.
objectives: Divide polynomials and apply the remainder and factor theorems.
Factor polynomials completely using the most efficient strategy.
Solve polynomial equations, finding real roots exactly or approximately.
Write equations for families of polynomial functions and particular members.
Solve polynomial inequalities graphically, with technology and algebraically.
Model and solve real-world problems with polynomial equations and inequalities.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 at a glance
lessons.body:
Everything in this chapter connects back to one statement — the **division statement** $P(x) = (x - b)Q(x) + R$.

| Idea | What it says | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Long / synthetic division | find $Q(x)$ and $R$ | 2.1, 2.2 |
| Remainder theorem | $R = P(b)$ (or $P(\frac{b}{a})$ for $ax - b$) | 2.1 |
| Factor theorem | $x - b$ is a factor $\iff P(b) = 0$ | 2.2 |
| Integral / rational zero theorems | which values of $b$ to test | 2.2 |
| Polynomial equations | factor, then zero product property | 2.3 |
| Families | $y = k(x - a_1)\cdots(x - a_n)$ | 2.4 |
| Inequalities (technology) | read intervals from the graph | 2.5 |
| Inequalities (algebra) | factor + sign table | 2.6 |

**Roots, zeros and $x$-intercepts** are the thread running through it all: the real roots of $P(x) = 0$ are the zeros of $P$, which are the $x$-intercepts of $y = P(x)$, which are the boundary points of the inequalities $P(x) > 0$ and $P(x) < 0$.

lessons.title: A complete factoring strategy
lessons.body:
When you meet a polynomial you need to factor (to solve an equation or inequality), work through this checklist:

1. **Common factor?** Take it out first — including a factor of $x$ or $-1$.
2. **Special pattern?** Difference of squares, sum or difference of cubes, perfect-square trinomial.
3. **Four terms?** Try grouping.
4. **Trinomial (including in $x^2$)?** Factor like a quadratic.
5. **Otherwise:** list possible rational zeros $\frac{b}{a}$, test them with the factor theorem, divide (synthetic division is fastest), and repeat on the quotient.
6. **Leftover quadratic that won't factor?** Quadratic formula — or the discriminant shows there are no real roots.

> Check your factorisation by expanding, or by substituting a value such as $x = 1$ into both forms.

lessons.title: Solving any polynomial inequality
lessons.body:
1. Rearrange so one side is $0$.
2. If it factors, factor completely; otherwise use technology to find the zeros (rounded as asked).
3. Mark the zeros on a number line — they create the intervals.
4. Decide the sign on each interval: test values, a sign table, or the end behaviour plus the orders of the zeros.
5. Pick the intervals that match the inequality. Use **closed** endpoints for $\le$ and $\ge$, **open** for $<$ and $>$.
6. In an application, intersect with the domain that makes sense, and answer in words with units.

**Quick sign shortcut:** for a polynomial with all zeros of order 1, the signs alternate. Start from the right: the right-most interval has the sign of the leading coefficient.

lessons.title: The most common mistakes in this chapter
lessons.body:
| Mistake | Fix |
|---|---|
| Substituting $x = 3$ for the divisor $x + 3$ | Solve divisor $= 0$: use $x = -3$ |
| Forgetting a placeholder ($0x^2$) | Write every power before dividing |
| Writing $Q(x) + R$ instead of $Q(x) + \frac{R}{x - b}$ | The remainder is also divided; state $x \neq b$ |
| Testing only integers when the leading coefficient isn't 1 | Use the rational zero theorem |
| Dividing an equation by $x$ | Factor $x$ out to keep the root $x = 0$ |
| Using an $x$-intercept to find $k$ in a family | Use a point **not** on the $x$-axis |
| Not flipping the sign when dividing by a negative | Flip it! |
| Assuming signs always alternate | Even-order zeros don't change sign |

keyTerms.definition: The remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $x - b$ is $P(b)$.
$x - b$ is a factor of $P(x)$ if and only if $P(b) = 0$.
Rational zeros have the form $\frac{b}{a}$, $b$ a factor of the constant term, $a$ a factor of the leading coefficient.
$y = k(x - a_1)\cdots(x - a_n)$: polynomial functions with the same zeros.
An inequality involving a polynomial; its solution is a union of intervals.
How many times its factor is repeated; even order → the graph touches the axis.

workedExamples.title: Checking statements about a polynomial
workedExamples.problem: For $P(x) = 5x^3 + 4x^2 - 3x + 2$, decide whether each statement is true: (A) the remainder when dividing by $x + 1$ is $8$; (B) $x + 2$ is a factor; (C) $P(-2) = -16$; (D) $P(x) = (x + 1)(5x^2 - x - 2) - 4$.
steps: (D) $(x + 1)(5x^2 - x - 2) = 5x^3 + 4x^2 - 3x - 2$, so $P(x) = (x + 1)(5x^2 - x - 2) + 4$. The statement has the wrong sign: **false** (it should be $+4$, matching (A)).

workedExamples.title: Unknown coefficient, then a second remainder
workedExamples.problem: $f(x) = x^4 + kx^3 - 2x^2 + 1$ leaves remainder $5$ when divided by $x + 2$. Find $k$, then the remainder when $f(x)$ is divided by $x + 4$.

workedExamples.title: Dimensions from specifications
workedExamples.problem: A box's width is $5$ cm less than its length and its height is $1$ cm more than double its width. The volume is $550$ cm³. Find the dimensions.
steps: Test factors of $550$: $P(10) = 2000 - 1900 + 450 - 550 = 0$ ✓. Divide: $(l - 10)(2l^2 + l + 55) = 0$; the quadratic has discriminant $1 - 440 < 0$.

misconceptions.myth: The remainder theorem tells you the quotient.
misconceptions.fact: It only gives the remainder; divide to get the quotient.
It has one, two or three (two when one zero has order 2).

misconceptions.myth: If $P(a) > 0$ and $P(b) > 0$, there is no zero between $a$ and $b$.
misconceptions.fact: There could be an even number of zeros between them (or a touching zero). A sign change guarantees a zero; no sign change guarantees nothing.
It is false at $x = 4$, where it equals $0$.

realWorld.title: Design and manufacturing
realWorld.body: Volume models for boxes and moulds lead to polynomial equations (exact sizes) and inequalities (acceptable ranges of sizes).

realWorld.title: Business
realWorld.body: Revenue and profit models give break-even points (roots) and profitable periods (inequality intervals).

realWorld.title: Entertainment engineering
realWorld.body: Ride heights over time are polynomial models; inequalities show when riders are above or below safety thresholds.

practice.question: Divide $x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x - 7$ by $x + 3$; write the quotient form, the restriction and the check statement.
Factor $x^3 + 9x^2 + 26x + 24$.
practice.hint: All coefficients positive, so try negative values.

practice.question: Determine the real roots of $(x^2 + 5)(x - 2) = 0$ and $(3x^2 - 27)(x^2 - 3x - 10) = 0$.
Find the family of cubics with zeros $1 \pm \sqrt3$ and $-2$, and the member through $(1, 9)$.

summary: Division statement: $P(x) = (x - b)Q(x) + R$; remainder theorem: $R = P(b)$.
Factor theorem: $P(b) = 0 \iff (x - b)$ is a factor. Use the integral and rational zero theorems to choose test values.
Solve polynomial equations by factoring completely; use the quadratic formula or technology when needed.
Families: $y = k(x - a_1)\cdots(x - a_n)$; one extra point gives $k$.
Polynomial inequalities: zeros split the axis into intervals; choose intervals by sign, include endpoints for $\le$, $\ge$.

questions.text:
For each division, (i) use the remainder theorem to find the remainder, and (ii) perform the division and write the result in quotient form with any restriction.

(a) $x^3 + 9x^2 - 5x + 3$ divided by $x - 2$

(b) $12x^3 - 2x^2 + x - 11$ divided by $3x + 1$
questions.modelAnswer:
**(a)** (i) $P(2) = 8 + 36 - 10 + 3 = 37$.

(ii) Synthetic division with $2$: $1, 9, -5, 3 \to 1, 11, 17, \mathbf{37}$.

$\dfrac{x^3 + 9x^2 - 5x + 3}{x - 2} = x^2 + 11x + 17 + \dfrac{37}{x - 2},\quad x \neq 2$

**(b)** (i) $3x + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -\tfrac13$. $P\left(-\tfrac13\right) = 12\left(-\tfrac1{27}\right) - 2\left(\tfrac19\right) - \tfrac13 - 11 = -\tfrac49 - \tfrac29 - \tfrac39 - \tfrac{99}{9} = -12$.

(ii) Long division: $12x^3 \div 3x = 4x^2$; subtract $12x^3 + 4x^2$ → $-6x^2 + x$; $-6x^2 \div 3x = -2x$; subtract $-6x^2 - 2x$ → $3x - 11$; $3x \div 3x = 1$; subtract $3x + 1$ → $-12$.

$\dfrac{12x^3 - 2x^2 + x - 11}{3x + 1} = 4x^2 - 2x + 1 - \dfrac{12}{3x + 1},\quad x \neq -\tfrac13$

rubric.point: (a) correct remainder by the remainder theorem
(b) correct long division and quotient form with restriction

questions.text: For $P(x) = 5x^3 + 4x^2 - 3x + 2$, a student claims: (A) dividing by $x + 1$ leaves remainder $8$; (B) $x + 2$ is a factor; (C) $P(-2) = -16$; (D) $P(x) = (x + 1)(5x^2 - x - 2) - 4$. Decide whether each claim is true. Correct every false claim and justify your decisions.
questions.modelAnswer:
(A) $P(-1) = -5 + 4 + 3 + 2 = 4$. **False** — the remainder is $4$.

(C) $P(-2) = 5(-8) + 4(4) - 3(-2) + 2 = -40 + 16 + 6 + 2 = -16$. **True**.

(B) By the factor theorem $x + 2$ is a factor only if $P(-2) = 0$, but $P(-2) = -16$. **False** — dividing by $x + 2$ leaves remainder $-16$.

(D) $(x + 1)(5x^2 - x - 2) = 5x^3 - x^2 - 2x + 5x^2 - x - 2 = 5x^3 + 4x^2 - 3x - 2$. To get $+2$ we must add $4$: $P(x) = (x + 1)(5x^2 - x - 2) + 4$. **False** (sign of the remainder).

rubric.point: Uses the factor theorem to reject (B)
Expands to check (D) and corrects it

questions.text: Let $f(x) = x^4 + kx^3 - 2x^2 + 1$. When $f(x)$ is divided by $x + 2$, the remainder is ${{R}}$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the remainder when $f(x)$ is divided by $x + 4$.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain how you could verify part (b) by division.

rubric.point: Describes a valid verification, mentioning the placeholder

questions.text: For what value of $b$ will the polynomial $P(x) = 4x^3 - 3x^2 + bx + 6$ have the same remainder when it is divided by $x - 1$ and by $x + 3$?

rubric.point: (b) finds a zero using the rational zero theorem and factors
(c) finds two zeros and divides twice correctly

questions.text: Rectangular blocks of limestone have volume, in cubic metres, $V(x) = 2x^3 + 7x^2 + 2x - 3$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Determine the dimensions of the blocks in terms of $x$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: What are the dimensions when $x = 1$? What is the volume?

parts.label: c
parts.text: What values of $x$ are possible? Explain.

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) Possible rational zeros: $\pm1, \pm3, \pm\tfrac12, \pm\tfrac32$. $V(-1) = -2 + 7 - 2 - 3 = 0$ → $x + 1$ is a factor.

Dividing: $V(x) = (x + 1)(2x^2 + 5x - 3) = (x + 1)(2x - 1)(x + 3)$.

Dimensions: $(x + 1)$ m, $(2x - 1)$ m, $(x + 3)$ m.

(b) When $x = 1$: $2$ m, $1$ m and $4$ m. Volume $8$ m³; check $V(1) = 2 + 7 + 2 - 3 = 8$ ✓

(c) Every dimension must be positive; the binding condition is $2x - 1 > 0$, so $x > \tfrac12$.

rubric.point: Finds a factor using the factor theorem
Correct dimensions when $x = 1$, with a check

questions.text: Determine $k$ so that $x - {{m}}$ is a factor of $x^3 + {{a}}x^2 - kx - {{c}}$. Show your check.

Use the graph of $y = P(x)$, a quartic polynomial with leading coefficient $1$, to determine the roots of $P(x) = 0$. Then write $P(x)$ in factored form and explain how the graph confirms the degree.

```plot
f: (x+{{A}})*(x+1)*(x-{{B}})*(x-{{C}})
domain: -6, 6
points: (-{{A}},0), (-1,0), ({{B}},0), ({{C}},0)
```
questions.modelAnswer:
The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x = -{{A}}$, $-1$, ${{B}}$ and ${{C}}$, so these are the roots.

$P(x) = (x + {{A}})(x + 1)(x - {{B}})(x - {{C}})$

Four distinct crossings (each a zero of order 1) and both ends pointing **up** match a quartic with a positive leading coefficient.

rubric.point: Writes the factored form with correct signs

questions.text: Determine the real roots of each equation: (a) $(5x^2 + 20)(3x^2 - 48) = 0$  (b) $(2x^2 - x - 13)(x^2 + 1) = 0$ (give exact roots and two-decimal approximations).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the positive root in (b) to two decimal places.

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $5x^2 + 20 = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 = -4$: no real roots. $3x^2 - 48 = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 = 16 \Rightarrow x = \pm4$. Real roots: $\pm4$.

(b) $x^2 + 1 = 0$: no real roots. $2x^2 - x - 13 = 0$: $x = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 104}}{4} = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{105}}{4}$, so $x \approx 2.81$ or $x \approx -2.31$.

questions.text: Solve $7x^3 + 5x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0$. Round answers to one decimal place where necessary.
questions.modelAnswer:
$P(-1) = -7 + 5 + 5 - 3 = 0$, so $x + 1$ is a factor.

Synthetic division with $-1$: $7, 5, -5, -3 \to 7, -2, -3, \mathbf{0}$.

$(x + 1)(7x^2 - 2x - 3) = 0$

$7x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 + 84}}{14} = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{88}}{14} = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{22}}{7}$

$x = -1$, $x \approx 0.8$, $x \approx -0.5$.

questions.text: The specifications for a cardboard box state that the width is $5$ cm less than the length, and the height is $1$ cm more than double the width. Write an equation for the volume and find the dimensions for a volume of $550$ cm³.
questions.modelAnswer:
Let the length be $l$. Width $= l - 5$; height $= 2(l - 5) + 1 = 2l - 9$.

$V = l(l - 5)(2l - 9) = 2l^3 - 19l^2 + 45l$

$2l^3 - 19l^2 + 45l - 550 = 0$

Test factors of $550$ (larger values make sense for a length): $P(10) = 2000 - 1900 + 450 - 550 = 0$ ✓

Dividing: $(l - 10)(2l^2 + l + 55) = 0$. Discriminant $1 - 440 < 0$, so $l = 10$ is the only real root.

Dimensions: $10$ cm × $5$ cm × $11$ cm. Check $10 \cdot 5 \cdot 11 = 550$ ✓

rubric.point: Correct expressions for width and height
Correct volume equation in standard form
Finds the root with the factor theorem
Justifies that there are no other valid roots

questions.text:
Which function does **not** belong to the same family as the others? Explain.

* A: $y = (x - 2)(x + 1)(2x - 6)$
* B: $y = -3(x + 1)(x - 3)(x - 2)$
* C: $y = 0.5(2x - 4)(x + 1)(x - 3)$
* D: $y = 4(x - 2)(x - 1)(x - 3)$
questions.modelAnswer:
Rewrite each factor as $(x - a)$:

* A: $2x - 6 = 2(x - 3)$ → $y = 2(x - 2)(x + 1)(x - 3)$: zeros $2, -1, 3$.
* B: zeros $-1, 3, 2$.
* C: $2x - 4 = 2(x - 2)$ → $y = (x - 2)(x + 1)(x - 3)$: zeros $2, -1, 3$.
* D: zeros $2, 1, 3$.

**D** does not belong: it has the zero $1$ instead of $-1$. A, B and C are members of $y = k(x - 2)(x + 1)(x - 3)$ with $k = 2, -3, 1$.

rubric.point: Rewrites factors to find the zeros
States the $k$ values / family for the others

questions.text: (a) Determine an equation, in simplified form, for the family of cubic functions with zeros $1 \pm \sqrt3$ and $-2$. (b) Determine the member of the family whose graph passes through $(1, {{y0}})$.

rubric.point: Correct quadratic factor from the irrational zeros

questions.text:
Determine an equation for the polynomial function represented by this graph. The $y$-intercept is $(0, {{-4*k}})$.

```plot
f: {{k}}*(x+2)*(x-1)^2*(x-2)
domain: -3, 3
points: (-2,0), (1,0), (2,0), (0,{{-4*k}})
```
questions.modelAnswer:
Zeros: $-2$ and $2$ (the graph crosses), and $1$ (the graph touches and turns back, so order 2). Degree $1 + 2 + 1 = 4$.

Family: $y = k(x + 2)(x - 1)^2(x - 2)$.

$y$-intercept: $k(2)(1)(-2) = -4k = {{-4*k}}$, so $k = {{k}}$.

$$y = {{k}}(x + 2)(x - 1)^2(x - 2)$$

rubric.point: Identifies zeros and the order-2 zero

questions.text:
Use technology to solve each inequality. Round the zeros to one decimal place.

(a) $x^3 - 2x^2 - 3x + 1 < 0$

(b) $2x^2 - x - 13 \ge 0$
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) Zeros of $y = x^3 - 2x^2 - 3x + 1$: $\approx -1.2$, $0.3$, $2.9$. Positive cubic → below the axis on $(-\infty, -1.2)$ and $(0.3, 2.9)$.

$x < -1.2$ or $0.3 < x < 2.9$

(b) Zeros $\approx -2.3$ and $2.8$. Parabola opens up → on or above the axis outside the zeros.

$x \le -2.3$ or $x \ge 2.8$

questions.text: The height of a roller coaster car above the ground is modelled by $h(t) = -0.1t^3 + 1.2t^2 - 2.5t + 6$, where $h$ is in metres and $t$ is in seconds, $0 \le t \le 10$. When is the car more than $10$ m above the ground?

parts.label: a
parts.text: For how long is the car above 10 m? (one decimal place)

questions.modelAnswer:
Solve $h(t) > 10$: $-0.1t^3 + 1.2t^2 - 2.5t - 4 > 0$.

Graph $y = -0.1t^3 + 1.2t^2 - 2.5t - 4$ (or $y = h(t)$ with $y = 10$). Zeros $\approx -1.0$, $4.5$, $8.5$.

Negative leading coefficient: the graph is above the axis between $4.5$ and $8.5$ (and for $t < -1.0$, outside the domain).

The car is above $10$ m for about $4.5 < t < 8.5$ seconds — roughly $4$ seconds in total.

rubric.point: Finds the relevant zeros with technology

questions.text: Solve each inequality algebraically and show the solution on a number line: (a) $(5x + 4)(x - 4) \ge 0$  (b) $-(2x + 3)(x - 1)(3x - 2) \le 0$  (c) $(x^2 + 4x + 4)(x^2 - 25) > 0$
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) Zeros $-0.8$, $4$. Opens up: $x \le -0.8$ or $x \ge 4$.

(b) Multiply by $-1$ and flip: $(2x + 3)(x - 1)(3x - 2) \ge 0$. Zeros $-1.5$, $\tfrac23$, $1$; positive cubic: $-, +, -, +$. Solution: $-1.5 \le x \le \tfrac23$ or $x \ge 1$.

(c) $(x + 2)^2(x - 5)(x + 5) > 0$. $(x + 2)^2 > 0$ for $x \neq -2$, so we need $(x - 5)(x + 5) > 0$ (and $x \neq -2$, which is automatic): $x < -5$ or $x > 5$.

rubric.point: (b) handles the negative and gets the correct intervals
(c) factors and uses the squared factor correctly

questions.text: Solve by factoring: (a) $12x^2 + 25x - 7 \le 0$  (b) $2x^3 + 5x^2 - 18x - 45 > 0$
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $(4x - 1)(3x + 7) \le 0$. Zeros $-\tfrac73$ and $\tfrac14$; opens up → between: $-\tfrac73 \le x \le \tfrac14$.

(b) $(2x + 5)(x - 3)(x + 3) > 0$. Zeros $-3, -2.5, 3$; positive cubic: $-, +, -, +$. Solution: $-3 < x < -2.5$ or $x > 3$.

From the factor theorem ($P(2) = 0$, $P(-2) = 0$) and division:

$-3x^4 + 10x^3 + 20x^2 - 40x - 32 = -(x - 2)(x + 2)(3x + 2)(x - 4)$

Zeros $-2, -\tfrac23, 2, 4$. Negative quartic → signs $-, +, -, +, -$.

$\le 0$: $x \le -2$ or $-\tfrac23 \le x \le 2$ or $x \ge 4$.

questions.text: (a) Describe the similarities and differences between polynomial **equations**, polynomial **functions** and polynomial **inequalities**. (b) What is the relationship between roots, zeros and $x$-intercepts? Support both answers with examples.
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) All three involve the same polynomial expression, e.g. $x^2 - x - 6$.
* **Function:** $f(x) = x^2 - x - 6$ — a rule giving an output for every input; it has a graph.
* **Equation:** $x^2 - x - 6 = 0$ — asks for specific values: $x = -2, 3$.
* **Inequality:** $x^2 - x - 6 < 0$ — asks for intervals: $-2 < x < 3$.
The equation's solutions are the function's zeros and the inequality's boundary points.

(b) The **roots** of $P(x) = 0$, the **zeros** of $P(x)$ and the **$x$-intercepts** of $y = P(x)$ are the same real numbers ($-2$ and $3$ here), seen as solutions, inputs giving 0, and points on a graph. Non-real roots are not $x$-intercepts.

rubric.point: Describes each of function, equation, inequality with examples
Explains roots/zeros/intercepts relationship with an example

questions.text: Boxes for chocolates are made from cardboard sheets $36$ cm by $20$ cm by cutting squares of side $x$ cm from each corner and folding. (a) Express the volume as a function of $x$. (b) Determine the dimensions for a volume of $450$ cm³ (to the nearest tenth). (c) Determine algebraically or with technology the values of $x$ for which the volume is at least $450$ cm³.
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $V(x) = x(36 - 2x)(20 - 2x) = 4x(18 - x)(10 - x)$, $0 < x < 10$.

(b) $V(x) = 450$: technology gives $x \approx 0.7$ or $x \approx 8.6$ in the domain.
* $x \approx 0.7$: $34.6$ cm × $18.6$ cm × $0.7$ cm
* $x \approx 8.6$: $18.8$ cm × $2.8$ cm × $8.6$ cm

(c) $V(x) - 450 \ge 0$: the zeros in the domain are $0.7$ and $8.6$, and $V(x) > 450$ between them (e.g. $V(3) = 4(3)(15)(7) = 1260$). So $0.7 \le x \le 8.6$ cm (approximately).

questions.text:
**Can you tell just by looking?** Consider $x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0$, $x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 = 0$ and $x^4 - 10x^3 + 35x^2 - 50x + 24 = 0$.

(a) Determine the roots of each equation. (b) Describe the pattern in the roots. (c) Make a conjecture about how the coefficients relate to the roots, and test it on $x^3 - 7x + 6 = 0$.
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $x^2 - 3x + 2 = (x - 1)(x - 2)$: roots $1, 2$.
$x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6$: $P(1) = 0$; dividing gives $x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3)$: roots $1, 2, 3$.
$x^4 - 10x^3 + 35x^2 - 50x + 24$: $P(1) = 0$ → quotient $x^3 - 9x^2 + 26x - 24$; $Q(2) = 0$ → $x^2 - 7x + 12 = (x - 3)(x - 4)$: roots $1, 2, 3, 4$.

(b) The roots are the consecutive integers $1, 2, \dots, n$.

(c) **Conjecture:** for a polynomial with leading coefficient $1$, the coefficient of $x^{n-1}$ is the **negative of the sum** of the roots ($-3 = -(1 + 2)$, $-6 = -(1 + 2 + 3)$, $-10 = -(1 + 2 + 3 + 4)$), and the constant term is $\pm$ the **product** of the roots ($2$, $-6$, $24$ — positive for even degree, negative for odd).

**Test:** $x^3 - 7x + 6 = 0$: $P(1) = 0$ → $(x - 1)(x^2 + x - 6) = (x - 1)(x + 3)(x - 2)$. Roots $1, 2, -3$: sum $0$, matching the $x^2$-coefficient $0$ ✓; product $-6$, and the constant is $+6 = -(-6)$ ✓ (odd degree).

rubric.point: Correct roots of all three equations
States a reasonable conjecture linking coefficients to sum/product of roots

questions.text: Write two possible quartic inequalities — one using $\le$ and one using $\ge$ — whose solution is $-2 - \sqrt3 \le x \le -2 + \sqrt3$ or ${{a}} \le x \le {{b}}$. Explain your reasoning.
questions.modelAnswer:
Boundary values: $-2 \pm \sqrt3$, ${{a}}$, ${{b}}$.

Pair the irrational ones: $(x + 2)^2 - 3 = x^2 + 4x + 1$. Other factors: $(x - {{a}})(x - {{b}})$.

The solution is two closed intervals **between** pairs of zeros, which is where a **positive** quartic is negative (pattern $+, -, +, -, +$).

* $\le$: $(x^2 + 4x + 1)(x - {{a}})(x - {{b}}) \le 0$
* $\ge$: $-(x^2 + 4x + 1)(x - {{a}})(x - {{b}}) \ge 0$

(Any positive multiple works too.) Test $x = 0$, which lies between $-2 + \sqrt3 \approx -0.27$ and ${{a}}$ and should be excluded: $(1)({{-a}})({{-b}}) = {{a*b}} > 0$, so it fails the $\le$ inequality ✓.

rubric.point: (c) two zeros found and full factorisation

questions.text: The volume of an open-top box made from a $40$ cm by $32$ cm sheet with corner squares of side $x$ is $V(x) = 4x(20 - x)(16 - x)$. (a) Write equations for boxes with twice and half this volume and explain how the three functions are related. (b) Find the values of $x$ for which the original box has volume greater than $2016$ cm³.
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) Twice: $V = 8x(20 - x)(16 - x)$; half: $V = 2x(20 - x)(16 - x)$. All three are members of the family $y = kx(x - 20)(x - 16)$ (with $k = 4, 8, 2$): same zeros, vertical stretches/compressions of one another.

(b) $4x^3 - 144x^2 + 1280x > 2016 \Rightarrow x^3 - 36x^2 + 320x - 504 > 0 \Rightarrow (x - 2)(x^2 - 34x + 252) > 0$.
Zeros $2$, $17 \pm \sqrt{37}$ ($\approx 10.9$, $23.1$). Positive on $(2, 10.9)$ within the domain $0 < x < 16$.

$2 < x < 17 - \sqrt{37} \approx 10.9$ cm.
